decisions.reason: The building data digital twin service remains strongly related to our geospatial integration capabilities, and our R&D and project learning should let us refine it in a growing market rather than withdraw it.

Authentication and identity delegation is adjacent to our core GeoIT stack and can still benefit from our integration know-how, but its less central fit keeps withdrawal risk higher than for core GIS offerings.

The open GIS application development framework deepens competencies we already possess in software components, standards, and customer-specific development, making continued retention the most likely course.
The GIS-focused identity and access service directly complements our installed base and customer workflows, so we are likely to keep commercializing and iterating it rather than exit.
The geodata business process consulting workshop builds directly on our consulting, training, and user-centered process expertise and requires little new knowledge beyond what we already absorb well.
